title: Map Skills: Calculations
summary: Calculate distance, area, average gradient, bearings and direction, and time and speed using topographic maps.

notes.caption: On a 1 : 50 000 map, 1 cm = 0,5 km; on a 1 : 10 000 orthophoto map, 1 cm = 0,1 km (100 m)

notes.title: Distance on a 1 : 50 000 map
notes.problem: The straight-line distance between two trigonometrical stations is 5,6 cm. Find the real distance in km and in m.

notes.caption: Convert each side to real distance FIRST, then multiply. Area is in km².

notes.title: Area of a block
notes.problem: A rectangular farm on a 1 : 50 000 map measures 4 cm by 3 cm. Calculate its real area.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: Do NOT multiply 4 × 3 = 12 cm² and then multiply by 0,5. Because area has two dimensions, each side must be converted separately.

**Gradient** describes how steep a slope is. It is the relationship between the **vertical interval (VI)**, the difference in height, and the **horizontal equivalent (HE)**, the horizontal distance. Both must be in the **same unit** (metres).

notes.title: Calculating gradient
notes.problem: Spot height A is 1 420 m and trig station B is 1 620 m. On a 1 : 50 000 map they are 4 cm apart. Calculate the average gradient from A to B.
notes.answer: 1 : 10 (for every 10 m forward, the land rises 1 m)

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: The bigger the second number, the gentler the slope. 1 : 5 is steeper than 1 : 50.

items: Draw a line from the starting point to the end point.
Draw a north line through the starting point, parallel to the map's grid lines.
Place your protractor on the starting point and measure the angle **clockwise from north** to the line.
Write it as three digits, e.g. 064°.

notes.text: **True bearing** is measured from true (geographic) north. **Magnetic bearing** is measured from magnetic north, which a compass points to; the difference is the **magnetic declination**, shown on topographic maps. In South Africa, magnetic north is west of true north, so magnetic bearing = true bearing + magnetic declination.

notes.title: Travel time
notes.problem: A road between two towns measures 12 cm on a 1 : 50 000 map. How long will a cyclist travelling at 20 km/h take?

On a 1 : 50 000 map, the horizontal distance between two points is 3 cm and the height difference is 75 m. Calculate the average gradient.
